newsitem.title: CHILE: Banco Santander Chile to boost market share.
newsitem.headline: Banco Santander Chile to boost market share.

text.p: After losing ground following last year's merger, Banco Santander Chile expects its share of the loan market to rise to 15 percent in the next few years, said Emilio Botin, president of Grupo Santander.

"We had a 14 percent market share (before the merger), but this dropped to 13 percent as we applied a conservative criteria to loans which led to a reduction in clients," said Botin at a joint news conference with Mauricio Larrain, vice president of Banco Santander Chile.
"We want this figure to rise to 15 percent."
Santander, Chile's largest foreign bank, expects that it will take a couple of years to recover market share lost since the merger, said Larrain.
"The bank should recover market share within two to three years and then we should continue forward especially in the small and medium-sized businesses and personal banking sectors," he said.
Banco Santander has spent the last year carrying out a detailed review of the loan portfolio inherited after its buy-out of Banco Osorno, the largest takeover in Chilean bank history.
The bank took a $10 million charge for provisions on the loans in the first quarter, and will make final provisions in the second quarter, said Larrain.
Santander is interested in expanding its presence in Chile, but is unlikely to buy another bank, said Botin.
"We continue looking at opportunities in Chile for buying another entity, if the conditions are right, but not a bank," said Botin.

Santander has already invested $1 billion in Chile, its largest single investment in Latin America. The region accounts for around half of the $6 billion the bank has invested outside Spain. ((-- Margaret Orgill, Santiago newsroom, 562-699-5595 x212))
